method: Constructed an ambient-authority threat model independently of the listed CoreDeps, then checked whether LN-02 would fail for each omitted authority. Separately modelled authoritative-store state versus rebuildable cache state for LN-06 and compared LN-09's success obligation with the sealed busy-timeout/idempotent-insert/write-then-link protocol.

resolves.A2-R1-01: PARTIAL: LN-04 has the correct lifetime-neutral negative shape, but the suite does not prove semantic neutrality until the capability boundary is closed.
resolves.A2-R1-02: ACCEPT: none of LN-01..10 intrinsically requires a resident host.
resolves.A2-R1-03: PARTIAL: LN-09 exercises the right same-project contention case but asserts both executions succeed, which the sealed busy-timeout protocol does not guarantee.
resolves.A2-R1-04: ACCEPT: deterministic equality preconditions are explicit.
resolves.A2-R1-05: ACCEPT: removing cachePolicy from the semantic API is correct.
resolves.A2-R1-06: REJECT: CoreDeps is not exhaustive and the signature has two storage authorities.
resolves.A2-R1-07: ACCEPT: decision source paths are resolvable.
resolves.A2-R1-08: ACCEPT: one-shot availability is correctly separated as a product obligation.
resolves.A2-R1-V11-01: BLOCKER: define the exact execution-core boundary and add or explicitly forbid ID/entropy, rule/contribution registry, external-process supervisor/sandbox, scheduler/executor/resource-meter, and diagnostics authorities.
resolves.A2-R1-V11-02: BLOCKER: LN-02 proves only that listed fields have no fallback; it cannot detect unlisted ambient process/env/fs/net/RNG/signal/thread-local/global-registry access. Add import/call-closure and runtime-denial conformance.
resolves.A2-R1-V11-03: BLOCKER: LN-06 must compare stores with identical authoritative ledger/evidence and different rebuildable cache state, not an undifferentiated populated store versus empty store.
resolves.A2-R1-V11-04: BLOCKER: LN-09 must permit a typed LEDGER.BUSY_TIMEOUT after bounded retries while still forbidding corruption, partial publication, or lost successful writes.

sealedPropertiesCovered.property: One re-entrant execution core has no lifetime discriminator and has identical semantics under one-shot and resident host lifetimes.
Storage integrity is provided by the storage protocol without requiring an external deployment coordinator.
An explicit dependency record is not a capability boundary while ambient imports and process authority remain available.

coreDepsAudit.signatureDefect: analyze(snapshot, plan, store, deps) supplies StoreHandle directly while CoreDeps also contains storeHandle. Two storage paths make ownership and LN-02 ambiguous.

missingOrUnresolvedAuthorities.why: RunId/ExecutionId creation must be deterministic, content-derived, or injected; ambient RNG defeats replay and equality tests.
A Plan identifies work, but executable implementations still need resolution. providerRegistry covers semantic providers, not necessarily rules and contributions.
Probe/external-scanner execution, child cancellation, and reaping cannot safely use ambient process APIs if the core includes execution.
Process-global pools and meters can cause cross-run interference and make budgets lifetime-dependent.
Either define diagnostics as progress-only and semantically inert or inject a separate bounded sink.

coreDepsAudit.ln02FalsePass: An implementation can satisfy LN-02 for every listed member while importing process.env, fs, net, crypto.randomUUID, signal handlers, a thread-local scope, or a global registry. Therefore LN-02 does not establish its stated completeness property.
coreDepsAudit.verdict: exhaustiveForV1_1 must be false until the boundary and negative authority tests are explicit.

ln06.requiredPrecondition: Both executions see byte-identical authoritative ledger, baseline, evidence, and derivation inputs; they differ only in disposable acceleration entries.
ln06.requiredAssertion: The core cannot observe store implementation type, cache warmth, hit rate, or presence except through fact/CAS operations whose semantic result is identical.
ln06.failureIfUnchanged: An empty store may omit authoritative baselines/history, so a digest difference would not prove a lifetime bug and an equality pass could hide cache authority.

ln09.matchesProtocol: Yes on ownership: contention is resolved by busy-timeout, idempotent insert, and write-then-link, not an external mutex.
ln09.overclaim: No on liveness: the protocol allows bounded retry exhaustion and LEDGER.BUSY_TIMEOUT. It guarantees integrity, not that both concurrent plans always complete successfully.
ln09.requiredOutcomeSet: Each contender either publishes one valid SealedRun or returns the typed operational busy-timeout; every successful write remains reachable, and no corrupt, partial, or lost publication is observable.

confidence.CoreDeps: high that exhaustiveness is unproven; medium on which missing authorities belong inside versus outside the core because its execution boundary is not specified

whatWouldChangeMyMind: A v1.2 capability-closure artifact that fixes the duplicate StoreHandle, defines the core boundary, makes ambient authority mechanically unreachable or test-failing, and rewrites LN-06/LN-09 with the stated preconditions and allowed outcomes.
knownLimitations: This reviews the conformance specification, not an implemented suite.
The exact process-sandbox API depends on whether Probe execution is inside the execution core; resolving that boundary is part of the blocker.
